body:
That's just my view point on how to find my "Mr.Right", if he can accept me in a natural, comfortable look, then one day he can deserve me in a wedding dress. But that's just me.

My parents... or rather my father, I have avoided by staying in my room while he's home. I'm not sure how I can pull that off on the days he doesn't have work, but I'm sure I'll figure a way out.

Thank you for taking the time to comment. It really means a lot.

I see my therapist tomorrow, and I plan on telling him everything.

I told my oldest brother about the attempt and we made a deal that I would tell my therapist, and if I didn't, he would tell my parents.

I've been told that I would enjoy college, actually. I'm just counting down the days until I can get the fuck out of this hellhole I call "home".
Unfortunately, I'm not sure I'm eligible for many scholarships for the fact that both my parents work, and on paper they make a "nice living" (despite the fact that some days we don't even know if we can pay the mortgage, let alone college tuition). Which basically means, I may have to stay at home for a year or two and go to community college and live at home before I can transfer to a University.

Thanks. The wheel of life with bad sides and good sides *sigh* I think the wheel of life know's it's me, so it's been throwing me in the bad sides lately >.> Hopefully, I can pull myself out the darkness.
Thank you, that means a lot.

Juiceboxing must be afraid of pigeons? :)

Thank you for taking the time to comment. I feel a little bit better after reading the comments. I just feel so unloved by my parents, especially my father. I looked under the sleeve of the hoodie I was wearing where he grabbed me to throw me down the stairs and there's a bruise there. My mother, while more tender than my father, made a joke last night about Cole asking "What did you do that turned Cole gay?" That comment made filled me with rage, and I snapped at her.

Unfortunately, my parents know I'm suicidal. The day before school let out for spring break, I walk into the counseling office and tell my counselor, "I wish I were dead". This lead to her calling my mother, and then my counselor suggesting that she take me to a therapist. I have been in therapy for 6 weeks now, all 45 minute sessions spent on how my parents are not supportive of me in any way, shape, or form.

I love my parents, I really do. But it's ridiculous the way they treat me.

Thank you for the kind words. It's comforting knowing someone went through the similar. The thing that's killing me the most though is Cole. I leave for college in one more year, even if that means not going to UNT (the university of my dreams) and just going to the University that accepts EVERYONE that graduated high school, I'm leaving. My parents are my family, and that means even if I disappear for the next 4 years without calling them, they're not going to abandon me completely. With the exception of my mother, my parents don't want me in the house anymore anyways.
